note: Rodent diabetes models predicted durable glucose lowering; patients on MK-0941 and AZD1656 lost the effect within months, and only later hepatoselective or dual-acting drugs held it.
label: T2D (GCK activators)

engagement.note: The first GK activators lowered blood glucose and improved glucose tolerance in several rodent diabetes models.
engagement.short: GKAs lower glucose in diabetic rodents
engagement.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Sibling compound (RO-28-1675), not a member.
engagement.judgement: Class model opened at the first GKA rodent paper; the compound is a non-member sibling.

engagement.note: MK-0941 cut post-challenge glucose up to 48% in dogs and mice; in insulin-treated patients 2-h postmeal glucose fell 37 mg/dL.
engagement.quote: Maximal placebo-adjusted least squares mean changes from baseline in A1C (baseline A1C 9.0%) and 2-h PMG were -0.8% and -37 mg/dL (-2 mmol/L), respectively.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. Fasting glucose did not move in patients.
engagement.judgement: No direct GK occupancy readout exists; the models' own readout was glucose, so the tier is downstream. Paired Eiki 2011 (same drug) with Meininger 2011.
engagement.magnitude_basis: post-challenge glucose: dog OGTT AUC -48% vs patient 2-h PMG -37 mg/dL

dose.note: Rodent models set the glucose-lowering doses; MK-0941 stayed effective over 16 days in mice and 4 days in dogs.
dose.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no stated human exposure target found.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the rodent model's dose basis.

dose.note: AZD1656 was dosed to titrated exposures, lowered glucose at first, then lost effect; the 4-month HbA1c endpoint failed.
dose.quote: Although initially favourable plasma glucose reductions were observed, there was a loss of effect over time with sustained AZD1656 treatment.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The model side is a sibling member (MK-0941); no published AZD1656 exposure target before the trial was found.
dose.magnitude_basis: sustained glucose lowering at efficacious exposure (mice 16 days) vs loss by 4 months in patients
dose.judgement: Dose follows efficacy (reached, failed, abandoned). Year is the NCT01152385 results posting, before the paper.

dose.note: A model fitted to patient multiple-dose data picked titrated Phase 2 doses of LY2599506; observed HbA1c and hypoglycaemia matched. Trials stopped on nonclinical safety findings.
dose.quote: The predictions were in reasonable agreement with the observed clinical data.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; both Phase 2 trials (NCT01024244, NCT01029795) were terminated early for nonclinical safety findings.
dose.judgement: Treated the semi-mechanistic model as a new dose model (model_change); it was built on patient Phase 1 data, not animals.
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted vs observed 3-month HbA1c and hypoglycaemia

efficacy.note: GK activators lowered glucose in several rodent diabetes models.
efficacy.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.

efficacy.note: MK-0941 met its 14-week HbA1c primary endpoint (-0.8%), but the response was gone by week 30.
efficacy.quote: At Week 14, A1C and 2-h postmeal glucose (PMG) improved significantly versus placebo with all MK-0941 doses.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c change at the primary time point

patient_trials.quote: Addition of AZD1656 (individually titrated) to metformin gave significant improvements in glycaemic control up to 4 months, although efficacy diminished over time.

efficacy.judgement: Primary endpoint governs, so the week-14 win is same; the 30-week loss is recorded as partial, not scored.

efficacy.note: AZD1656 monotherapy missed its 4-month HbA1c primary endpoint after early glucose falls faded; rodent models had shown sustained lowering.
efficacy.quote: The changes from baseline to 4 months in HbA1c were not significant for the AZD1656 40-200 mg group versus placebo [mean (95% CI) placebo-corrected change: -0.22 (-0.65, 0.20)%; p = 0.30].
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. AstraZeneca later ran its own rodent models for up to 11 months and found durable lowering 'in marked contrast to clinical findings' (Baker 2014, doi 10.1111/bph.12504).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sustained glucose lowering in rodents vs non-significant 4-month HbA1c in patients
efficacy.judgement: One drug's contra beats MK-0941's same on the same rodent model. Baker 2014 is a retrodiction that also failed (contra) and confirms the call; not entered separately to avoid a repeat status.

efficacy.model: People with GCK-activating or GKRP loss-of-function variants
efficacy.note: TTP399 was designed from human genetics to activate liver GK only; it cut HbA1c 0.9% over 6 months without hypoglycaemia. Dorzagliatin later met two Phase 3 primaries.
efficacy.quote: In this 6-month study, TTP399 (800 mg/day) was associated with a clinically significant and sustained reduction in glycated hemoglobin, with a placebo-subtracted least squares mean HbA1c change from baseline of -0.9% (P < 0.01).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; sponsor-authored review of its own program. AGATA (NCT02405260) has no posted results; primary endpoint per registry is HbA1c change.
efficacy.judgement: Counted the human-genetic rationale as a new model (model_change); the paper sets rationale and trial side by side (comparison_stated). Dorzagliatin Phase 3s added as patient_trials since they change no status.

patient_trials.quote: At week 24, the least-squares mean change in glycated hemoglobin from baseline (95% confidence interval) was -1.07% (-1.19%, -0.95%) in the dorzagliatin group and -0.50% (-0.68%, -0.32%) in the placebo group
In patients with T2D who experienced inadequate glycemic control with metformin alone, dorzagliatin resulted in effective glycemic control with good tolerability and safety profile

safety.note: Rodent diabetes models carried the class into patients; early papers report efficacy, not lipid or liver harm.
safety.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no nonclinical toxicology review available (no member has an FDA NDA).

safety.note: After MK-0941 raised triglycerides in patients, nine GKAs raised hepatic and plasma lipids and caused fatty liver in db/db mice and rats.
safety.quote: MK-0941 was associated with an increased incidence of hypoglycemia and elevations in triglycerides and blood pressure.
safety.judgement: De Ceuninck (print 2013) postdates the MK-0941 triglyceride signal (2011), so it is a retrodiction. Hypoglycaemia and blood pressure not scored: no model statement found.

safety.note: The rodent lipid warning held prospectively for dorzagliatin, which raised hyperlipidaemia risk in a trial meta-analysis; fatty liver itself was not shown in patients.
safety.quote: Notably, dorzagliatin had significant effects on the occurrence of hyperlipidemia (OR 1.476, 95% CI 1.025-2.126) and hyperuricemia (OR 2.727, 95% CI 1.523-4.883) in the subgroup analyses.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Tier 4 meta-analysis; hepatic steatosis was not measured in the pooled trials; AstraZeneca's rodent models (Baker 2014) showed no triglyceride rise.
safety.reason: Lipid harm predicted, seen in patients
safety.judgement: First prospective test after the retrodiction: the 2013 warning predates dorzagliatin's Phase 3 data. Partial agreement (lipids yes, steatosis unmeasured) kept as same with partial.
safety.magnitude_basis: hyperlipidaemia odds ratio vs rodent plasma/hepatic triglycerides
